claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit substantial chemical complexity and variability across a vast composition space.
A newly developed computational potential can accurately determine the melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
The computational potential can accurately determine the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
The computational potential can accurately determine the entropy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
The computational potential can accurately determine the volume change at melting in high-entropy alloys.
The computational potential can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed computational potential can determine these thermodynamic properties efficiently.
The proposed potential can be based on DFT or molecular-dynamics simulations.
The proposed approach is applicable across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Trial-and-error experimental methods are costly and time-consuming for screening the large composition space of high-entropy alloys.
Prior computational methods have limited accuracy, efficiency, or applicability for the targeted melting and liquid-state properties.
Agreement between predicted and experimental melting and liquid-phase properties can be used to validate the proposed approach.
A significant deviation between predicted and experimental thermodynamic properties would falsify the hypothesis.
